headline: Khomeyni proclaims the Islamic Republic of Iran
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report for April 1979 carried, under its Iran heading, reportage on the referendum on an Islamic Republic: a ministry statement on balloting, extra ballot supplies, a Khomeyni statement after voting, and balloting in Kordestan.

headline: Argentina seizes the Falkland (Malvinas) Islands
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 2 April 1982 opened its Argentina section with the landings: forces moving into the disputed South Atlantic islands, a junta communique, a 'Malvinas Governor' named, a charge at the UN and claims of Soviet support.

headline: UN Security Council demands Argentine withdrawal from the Falklands
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of April 5, 1982, listed Nicaragua's response to a U.S. veto at the UN, D'Escoto addressing the Security Council, and a report on Argentina's Falklands takeover; no item on the Security Council's withdrawal demand.
doubt: Page lists a Falklands takeover report and Nicaraguan UN items, not the Security Council demand for Argentine withdrawal.

headline: US Commerce Secretary Ron Brown killed in air crash near Dubrovnik
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of April 4, 1996, listed under Croatia Tudjman appointing a commission to probe the Brown crash and cancelling his engagements after the air crash, both from Zagreb Radio.

headline: Pakistan hangs former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 4 April 1979 listed under Pakistan an official announcement on Bhutto's hanging, next to Zia's nuclear-free-zone proposal to India's Desai.

headline: France expels 47 Soviet diplomats and officials for espionage
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 5 April 1983 carried Paris AFP in English on France ordering 47 Soviet diplomats and officials out, 'the biggest intelligence clean-up' in Franco-Soviet relations, with a Moscow source confirming the TASS Paris bureau chief was among them.

headline: Bomb wrecks La Belle discotheque in West Berlin
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 7 April 1986 carried Moscow TASS in English on the La Belle blast: two dead, some 150 injured including 30 to 50 Americans, framed around the Soviet Union's stated rejection of terrorism 'in all its manifestations'.

headline: Kuwait Airways Flight 422 hijacked to Mashhad
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 6 April 1988 listed under Kuwait further reportage on the hijacking of the Boeing 747, with a Saudi SPA 'source' voicing concern and the Iraqi government condemning the hijack of the Kuwaiti plane.

headline: Thousands of Cubans crowd into the Peruvian Embassy in Havana
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 7 April 1980 carried Paris AFP and Madrid EFE from Havana: a 'human wave' of Cubans flocking into the Peruvian Embassy grounds after Havana said they could leave, more than 2,000 inside by evening.

headline: Presidents of Rwanda and Burundi killed as their plane is shot down
United States breaks diplomatic relations with Iran
fbis: The South Asia Daily Report of April 8, 1980, listed Iran's Revolution Council meeting discussing the break with the U.S., its communique on relations, militants pleased with sanctions, and the effects of Carter's moves.

headline: Soviet nuclear submarine Komsomolets sinks in the Norwegian Sea
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 10 April 1989 carried Moscow TASS in English: a fire aboard a nuclear-powered submarine southwest of Bear Island, sinking at more than 1,500 metres, loss of life, and Yazov ruling out radioactive contamination.

headline: Fighting spreads in Bosnia-Herzegovina after recognition
Macedonia admitted to the United Nations under a provisional name
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of April 9, 1993, carried a Macedonian address declaring that the republic, "now, as an equal member" of the United Nations, would uphold the UN Charter.

headline: Soviet troops break up a demonstration in Tbilisi, killing nineteen
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of April 10, 1989, carried TASS on the fourth day of unrest in Tbilisi on April 8, with mass rallies outside the government building; it does not report the April 9 crackdown.
doubt: Page covers the rallies of 8 April, before the troops broke up the demonstration.
excluded: Run-up only; rallies before the crackdown

headline: Georgia declares independence from the Soviet Union
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of April 10, 1991, carried presidential spokesman Ignatenko saying Gorbachev's reaction to Georgia's declaration of independence would follow the constitution's articles on leaving the union.

headline: Noriega convicted of drug trafficking in Miami
Ojhri Camp ammunition depot explodes in Rawalpindi
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 11 April 1988 listed under Pakistan the Rawalpindi depot fire: Defense Ministry statement, casualty figures, a U.S. bomb squad arriving, and Delhi radio saying sabotage was not ruled out and the depot lay near a nuclear site.

headline: South African Communist Party leader Chris Hani assassinated
fbis: The East Asia Daily Report of April 12, 1993, carried Seoul YONHAP on grounded F-16s and a new envoy to China; nothing on South Africa.
doubt: Page has only South Korean items; Hani's assassination does not appear.

headline: Idi Amin's regime falls as Tanzanian-backed forces take Kampala
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 13 April 1979 carried Moscow Domestic Service in Russian: the Uganda National Liberation Front and Tanzanian troops held Kampala and Yusuf Lule headed a provisional government, while Amin claimed to control 90 percent of the country.

headline: Albanian leader Enver Hoxha dies
fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of 11 April 1985 opened its Albania section with ATA reporting Enver Hoxha's death, followed by the funeral commission, national mourning, a 15 April funeral date and a medical bulletin.

headline: Samuel Doe seizes power in Liberia; President Tolbert killed
fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of 14 April 1980 listed under Liberia 'President Tolbert Overthrown by Armed Forces', then a run of coup-council items: curfew, arrest orders, a cabinet list, and a call to halt random shooting.

headline: Moscow admits the NKVD carried out the Katyn massacre
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 13 April 1990 carried Warsaw PAP in English: the USSR had admitted the NKVD murdered some 15,000 Polish officers at Katyn, calling it 'one of the most horrifying Stalinist crimes', as relayed via the BBC and Moscow radio.

headline: Geneva Accords on Afghanistan signed
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 14 April 1988 listed Afghanistan and Pakistan items on the accords: Junejo addressing the nation, Zia and Junejo hailing the agreement, and refugees in Iran protesting the Geneva agreements.

headline: Iraqi-linked plot to kill former President Bush in Kuwait
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 16 April 1993 carried Iraqi opposition claims, via KUNA and Kurdish clandestine radio, of attacks on Ba'th officials in Baghdad; nothing on a plot against Bush.
doubt: Page covers Iraqi opposition attacks inside Iraq, not the plot against former President Bush.

headline: US warplanes bomb Tripoli and Benghazi
fbis: The Middle East & South Asia review of 15 April 1986 led with the U.S. raids: Tripoli radio claimed over 20 U.S. planes downed and vowed to kill captured pilots, while reports differed on whether Qadhdhafi was hurt and on 'dozens' or 'hundreds' of casualties.

headline: Former Chinese party leader Hu Yaobang dies
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 17 April 1989 carried Moscow TASS in English citing XINHUA's obituary: Hu Yaobang, 'a prominent party official and statesman', had died that morning of a heart attack, with a brief career sketch.

headline: Israeli commandos assassinate PLO leader Abu Jihad in Tunis
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 18 April 1988 listed reactions to Abu Jihad's killing across North Africa: Qadhdhafi's condolences, Sudan denouncing the assassination, a Tunisian committee investigating, and a Kuwaiti cabinet session on the death.

headline: British policewoman shot dead from the Libyan People's Bureau in London
fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of 17 April 1984 carried Tripoli Domestic Service in Arabic accusing British police and 'agents of the British intelligence' of storming the Libyan People's Bureau in London and opening fire.

headline: El Al bomb plot foiled at Heathrow
fbis: The Middle East and South Asia review of April 21, 1986, carried further reportage on the attempted attack on an El Al airliner in London: Israel blaming Abu Nidal and Qadhdhafi, and the Jordanian suspect's arrest on April 18.

headline: Suicide bombing destroys the US Embassy in Beirut
fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of 18 April 1983 carried Beirut's Voice of Lebanon and Beirut Domestic Service: a car with a fake diplomatic plate crashed the U.S. Embassy entrance and exploded, with 20 employees and 5 marines reported killed.

headline: US Navy strikes Iranian oil platforms and warships (Operation Praying Mantis)
fbis: The Near East & South Asia review of 18 April 1988 reported IRNA on U.S. fire against the Nasr and Salman platforms, Iran calling for a 'holy defense against the U.S. invasion', and Iranian counterattacks on a Gulf oil platform and British barge.

headline: Israeli shelling kills over 100 at the UN post at Qana
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 19 April 1996 carried Cairo MENA: Foreign Minister Musa condemned Israel's strikes after the killing at Qana, where shelling of the Fijian UN contingent killed or wounded more than 150 sheltering civilians.

headline: Bombing of the federal building in Oklahoma City
fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of 20 April 1995 listed Israeli leaders offering aid to Clinton over the Oklahoma City blast and, under Lebanon, Al-Hariri condemning a 'criminal act' and a Shiite leader denouncing the bombing.

headline: Soviet fighters force down Korean Air Lines Flight 902 near Murmansk
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 21 April 1978 carried Moscow TASS on an 'unidentified plane' violating Soviet airspace near Murmansk and landing on a lake near Kem, plus Seoul radio citing Kosygin that two people died in the landing.

headline: Car bomb at Colombo bus station kills over 100
fbis: The South Asia Daily Report of 21 April 1987 listed under Sri Lanka a 'huge' explosion ripping through Colombo's bus station, citing Delhi radio and AFP, with curfew details and a death toll reaching 110.

headline: Chechen leader Dzhokhar Dudayev killed by a Russian missile strike
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of April 22, 1996, carried ITAR-TASS and INTERFAX on Defense Minister Grachev's April 19 Duma remarks on Chechen peace-plan losses; nothing on Dudayev's death.
doubt: Page covers the Duma debate on Russian military losses, not Dudayev's death.
excluded: Grachev's April 19 remarks, before the strike

headline: Memorial for Hu Yaobang as students fill Tiananmen Square
Sewer explosions devastate Guadalajara
Former President Richard Nixon dies
fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of 25 April 1994 carried Mexico City NOTIMEX: President Salinas sent condolences to Nixon's daughters, noting that Nixon, 81, died after a stroke and had stepped down over Watergate.

headline: Namibia admitted to the United Nations
fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of 24 April 1990 carried Belgrade TANJUG: Yugoslav Foreign Secretary Loncar opened his UN General Assembly speech by greeting Namibia as the newest member, its independence marking an end of the colonial era.

headline: Gorbachev and nine republic leaders agree the Novo-Ogarevo statement
fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of 24 April 1991 carried Moscow TASS: spokesman Ignatenko said that as he briefed, Gorbachev was meeting at Novo-Ogarevo with leaders of nine republics willing to sign a new union treaty, Yeltsin among them.

headline: US hostage rescue mission ends in disaster at Desert One, Iran
fbis: The South Asia Daily Report of 25 April 1980 carried AFP: Iranian leaders ordered a probe into the White House announcement of two aircraft crashing on a rescue mission, and Iranian radio said divine protection 'wrecked the American action'.

headline: Carter announces the failure of the Iran hostage rescue mission
fbis: The South Asia Daily Report of 25 April 1980 carried AFP reports of Iran's reaction to Carter's announcement, including a militant at the embassy telling NHK he did not trust the White House account and that the hostages were well.

headline: Israel completes its withdrawal from Sinai
fbis: The Middle East & South Asia review of 26 April 1982 reported Cairo radio and MENA on Egyptian flags raised at Rafah and Sharm ash-Shaykh, the IDF completing its Sinai withdrawal, and Jerusalem radio on the demolition and evacuation of Yamit.

headline: Russians vote in Yeltsin's confidence referendum
fbis: The Central Eurasia Daily Report of 26 April 1993 carried an ITAR-TASS press review calling Sunday's all-Russia referendum the papers' principal topic, with worries about turnout and ROSSIYSKAYA GAZETA judging Yeltsin still held 'tangible prestige'.

headline: Reactor explodes at Chernobyl
fbis: The Eastern Europe Daily Report of 29 April 1986 listed how each bloc capital relayed the news: Bratislava noting the 'Kiev accident', ADN citing TASS, Budapest reporting it, and Warsaw citing TASS and a 'radioactive cloud'.

headline: Communist coup in Afghanistan (the Saur Revolution)
fbis: The Middle East & North Africa Daily Report of 28 April 1978 carried Paris AFP from Islamabad: Kabul radio announced President Daud overthrown by an armed forces revolutionary council after fighting with tanks and MiG jets around the palace.

headline: Mujahidin leader Mojaddedi takes power in Kabul
fbis: The Near East & South Asia front page of 28 April 1992 reported Kabul Radio and AFP on Mojaddedi arriving in Kabul amid celebratory gunfire to assume the interim presidency of the Islamic State of Afghanistan, declaring a general amnesty.

headline: Cyclone devastates coastal Bangladesh
fbis: The Near East & South Asia contents for May 1991 listed Islamabad Radio on Pakistan's prime minister leaving for Bangladesh with aid, returning from Dhaka, and announcing a grant for cyclone victims.

headline: Riots break out in Los Angeles after the King verdict
Gunmen seize the Iranian Embassy in London
fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of 1 May 1980 carried AFP: Qotbzadeh said Iran would never bow to the 'terrorists' holding 20 hostages at its London embassy, while three Arab-Iranian groups in Beirut claimed the seizure.
